title: THE FIRE THAT KNEW HOW TO BURN
deck: An eighty-one-year-old woman has lit forty-one small fires on a hill the fire service wants emptied, and the only way to prove she is right is to find the one place her map is wrong.
shape: Six scenes across one afternoon and evening: a pattern read as a crime, a kitchen where the pattern is explained, a test the chief can stop, a gully nobody had burned, a wind that turns on time, and a report that begins with an old woman's map.

scenes.title: Burns by the Wall
paragraphs: *Sorrel Gate, upper terraces · 12:40*

Smoke stood on the western ridge, six kilometres off and leaning toward them. The district had given Sorrel Gate until three o'clock. Illuminara had spent the morning walking the upper terraces with a tablet of creek gauges, which was what the regional water office had sent her to do, and she had stopped doing it at the first black patch.

There were forty-one of them now. Each was the size of a tablecloth. Each was still warm when she held her palm an inch above it. None lay in open grass. Every one lay on the sheltered side of a drystone wall or the lip of a terrace, and not one had crossed the stone.
*Someone is counting the wind,* she thought. *Someone is lighting only where the wind has been refused.*

Taavi Brandt came up the track with a drip torch hanging unlit from his belt and a young crew lead named Joss Marren a pace behind. He was fifty-odd and broad, with the stillness of a man who had learned to spend his words last.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Somebody has been lighting my hill since six this morning. Eleven fires I can account for. I'd put the rest on the same hand.

**Illuminara**  
Forty-one. I've walked them all.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Then you've walked forty-one places where a fire could have got away from a person. Constable Hale is at the church with an order for Ivet Corrandon. She's eighty-one, she won't open her door to my crews, and at dark I carry her down that road myself. I would sooner she walked.

**Illuminara**  
Look at where they are, Chief. Not at who.
He looked, because he was fair and because she had said it quietly. He looked at the nearest patch and the wall above it, and for the length of a breath he said nothing.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Calder Fold. Nine years ago. I lit a backburn, lawful and signed, in a wind that behaved for four hours. In the fifth it veered and the fire took the track and then a barn, and there was a man asleep in the barn. Aldous Penn. Careful fires are the ones that kill people. The careless ones don't last long enough.

**Illuminara**  
Then I won't argue that she's careful. I'll ask whether she's right, and look for an instrument that can answer without either of us having to believe anything. Let me speak to her first.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Until two. At two the buses load, and she's on one or she's on my shoulder.

scenes.title: What the Hill Was For
paragraphs: *Corrandon cottage, kitchen · 13:15*

The door was not locked. Illuminara knocked anyway, and a voice told her through the wood that it never was, that people simply believed it was, and that she could come in if she had the sense to wipe her boots.

Ivet Corrandon sat at the table with ash to the elbows, a match tin at her right hand and a blackthorn stick against her chair. Across her left palm ran a blister the width of a finger. She had the face of someone who had been right for a long time without anyone's help.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
You're the water girl. They said a water girl was on my walls with a machine.

**Illuminara**  
I'm a water-modeller. The machine is a tablet and mostly it counts creeks. May I sit?

**Ivet Corrandon**  
If you've come to take me to the bus you can sit on the floor.

**Illuminara**  
I've no authority to take you anywhere. I came to ask about the wall at the top of Pellam's field.

The old woman looked at her for some time. Illuminara took the clean cloth from the dresser while she waited and asked, with her eyes, about the hand. A question can wait and a blister cannot. Ivet let her do it, watching with open suspicion and then, slowly, with less.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
In nineteen eighty-four a forestry man stood in this kitchen and told my Edrin the hill must not be burned, not by anyone, not ever, and he took the paper that said we could. Edrin was fined. He didn't speak for a week. Forty years we've lived under a hill with nothing to do but grow.

**Illuminara**  
And you went on burning.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
Small. At the end of the wet, on the lee of the walls. Edrin called it combing. A fire that comes over a ridge is hungry, and it eats everything between itself and the next thing to eat. Comb the lee of a wall black and the headfire reaches the stone, looks over, and finds nothing for its mouth. A wall with no black behind it is only a stack of stones.

**Illuminara**  
Then why not tell the chief?

**Ivet Corrandon**  
He lit a hill once and a man died. I read it in the paper. He'll hear old woman, and he'll hear liability, and he will not hear wall.
She said it without cruelty, as she might have given the weight of a loaf. Illuminara had been wrong about nothing in this kitchen so far, and she had the feeling that would not last.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
And you. Your machine has never smelled a slope at four o'clock. It's never stood where the air changes its mind.

**Illuminara**  
No, it hasn't. So tell me where your map is wrong. I would rather find that here than on the ridge.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
Nowhere.
The silence went on long enough for the kettle to tick. Ivet looked at the dressed hand, and at the stick, and at the window.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
The north. The gully above the Marrick cottages. I ran out of knee. Edrin never combed the gully. He said it burns itself. Then he never said another word about it, and I never asked.

Something turned over in Illuminara, quietly, like a key in a lock she had been leaning on for three weeks. The gully was the old stone leat, the flood channel she had modelled for the water office. Every storm she had run went down that cut like thread into a needle. *Water finds it. So does anything else that wants to go downhill.*

**Illuminara**  
Mrs Corrandon, would you tell me the order you burn in? Not the reasons. The order. I'll carry it to the chief as something he can test, with his own torch, on his own say.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
And if his test says I'm a fool?

**Illuminara**  
Then a fool's mistake is corrected in thirty metres, instead of a village's in three hundred. Either way the hill is the winner.

scenes.title: A Test He Could Stop
paragraphs: *Sorrel Gate school, command post · 14:05*

Two buses idled in the car park with their doors open. Brandt stood over a trestle table with the district map pinned under four stones, and he did not look up until she had laid her tablet on top of his county. Over his shoulder, Joss Marren was loading a hose reel and trying not to listen.

**Illuminara**  
She isn't lighting fires. She's combing the lee of every wall so a headfire has nothing to eat behind the stone. It's a firebreak drawn in fire. Forty years old, and the state forbade it for all of them.

**Taavi Brandt**  
That's what she says.

**Illuminara**  
It's what the walls say. I read them as load paths, and a load path is an interpretation, and she could be right by accident. So I'm not asking you to believe her. I'm asking for one segment. Thirty metres of the east wall, your crew, your torch, your hose behind it. If the burn does not die at the lee by itself, you put it out and we've lost twenty minutes.

**Taavi Brandt**  
And if it dies by itself, I've learned about one wall. The headfire isn't one wall.

**Illuminara**  
No. But it's a way of turning a coincidence into a measurement. And I'd ask you to hold the second thing against it as well, because I think she's right about the walls and I'm afraid of the place she hasn't burned.
He took a long time. A bus driver coughed. Outside, a woman was counting children from the school into the first coach, name by name, getting each name right.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Then these are mine. The buses go at three, all of them, nobody comes off. Anyone not on a bus is crew or on a tanker. The wind goes southwest at about twenty to six. I have one number and it does a different job in each hour. Before a torch is lit, thirty-five on the ridge gauge cancels the burn. After it's lit and the strip has gone cold, a gust past thirty-five or one ember across a wall, and nobody lights anything more: every crew comes off the walls and the Marrick track and stands behind the car park wall, and the black and the wet are left to do the work. I don't chase a headfire with a hose. And the woman stays where I can see her. Not in cuffs. At my shoulder.

**Illuminara**  
She'll want that. She'll want to be told what she's looking at.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Hale takes her statement afterwards. She isn't pardoned. If this goes wrong at Calder's rate, I'll want it said that I heard her and chose it, not that she tricked me.
Ivet had arrived at the car park door without being noticed, which at eighty-one and with a stick took talent. She stood in the frame and heard the last of it.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
I never asked to be pardoned, Chief.

**Taavi Brandt**  
No. I'm told you never asked anyone for anything. That's most of what's wrong with this.

scenes.title: The Gully
paragraphs: *East wall, then the gully head · 16:05*

Joss Marren lit thirty metres of the lee at ten past four, with Brandt crouched at his elbow and Ivet in a borrowed folding chair on the track above, her stick across her knees like a sword she had decided not to draw. The flame crept three paces along the grass. It lay down against the stone and went out.
Nobody said anything. A second pass, a little further along: the same. Joss looked at his chief. Brandt put two fingers into the black and held them there.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Cold.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
Of course it's cold. It had nothing to ask for.

Then the smoke from the last small patch did something that Illuminara had been waiting for and did not enjoy being right about. It did not lift. It slid sideways along the ground, thin and grey, leaning north, and went into the mouth of the gully above the Marrick cottages the way water goes into a drain.

**Illuminara**  
Chief, look at the smoke. That's my creek. The gully is the old leat, and it is the same shape for air that it is for water. When the wind goes southwest at twenty to six, the headfire won't come at the village over the walls she's combed. It'll come to the one place that has no black behind it, and the leat will take it straight down the cut and out over the top terrace.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Into the school and the Marrick cottages.

**Illuminara**  
Into both. And it won't stop at the wall, because no one has burned anything behind that wall for forty years.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
Edrin said it burns itself.

**Illuminara**  
When did he say it?

**Ivet Corrandon**  
The year after the goats went. Hennie Marrick kept sixty goats on that cut and they ate everything to the clay. Edrin said what he saw. He didn't say the goats had been doing the burning for us.
It was the first time Illuminara had seen the old woman look surprised, and she did not look away from it, out of courtesy. Forty years of a rule that had been right on the day it was spoken.

**Taavi Brandt**  
I can't backburn it dry. Not with a headfire two hours out. Dry fuel in a cut that draws like that, I'd be lighting my own chimney.

**Illuminara**  
Then don't burn it dry. The leat has a sluice at the head, and the creek is still running. Forty litres a second for the wet band, down the floor of the cut and over both banks, and a margin either side that your crew combs slow and downhill, Mrs Corrandon's way. A wet strip, a black strip, a wall. The fire has a river on one side and a stone on the other and nowhere to go but out.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Downhill. Not up. You said up in your notes.

**Illuminara**  
I did.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Up and you're feeding it a ramp. Thirty years I've never lit upslope. Down, a flame has to work for every metre.

**Illuminara**  
Down. Thank you.
She put her finger on his map, on the thin blue cut above the Marrick cottages, and gave him the numbers one at a time so that he could argue with each.

**Illuminara**  
Two hundred and forty metres from the sluice to the Marrick fence, three terraces, the third at a hundred and eighty. Eleven minutes a hundred metres. Open the sluice at ten to five and the wet front is past the third terrace at ten past. If it isn't, nobody lights the margins, and the crews go to the car park wall. That's the one failure signal, and it comes before any fire does. The wet and the black can run as far as the fence and no further. The two cottages sit forty metres beyond it, past any water I can carry. I would rather say that now than have you find it at six.

**Taavi Brandt**  
And the wall we just burned?

**Illuminara**  
Proves one wall. It's why I trust the margins and not the hill. The hill I'll know when the gully tells us, and I'll tell you what to look for. If I'm right, the headfire enters the head of the cut and slows to a crawl on the wet band. If I'm wrong, it won't slow, and you'll see flame standing on a bank. Either of us can see that from the car park wall.

The wheel at the sluice head had not turned since before Illuminara had been in the district. It took Joss and two of Brandt's volunteers and a length of scaffold pipe for a lever, and she stood by with her watch and counted them through it aloud, as one counts a woman in labour. At ten to five the stone throat filled and the cut began to talk.
At ten past five the wet front shone past the third terrace and the ridge gauge read eighteen. Brandt looked at the one number and then at the other.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Light.
Joss went down the east bank with the slow torch and the second crew down the west, walking downhill, a flame having to work for every metre.

scenes.title: The Wind Comes Round
paragraphs: *Car park wall, below the gully · 17:39*
The wind turned a minute early.

It came off the west like a door opening in a long house, and the smoke that had leaned north for three hours stood up, thought about it, and leaned the other way. The ridge gauge on Brandt's radio read twenty-nine, then thirty-three. His crews were still in their lines: black behind every wall, a wet band shining down the bottom of the cut, a combed margin either side with the last embers of Joss's slow torch still ticking in it.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Thirty-four. Nothing left to light, so the other half of my number is the one that counts now. One more and they come off, walking, not asking. Joss, tell them the figure. I want them already turned.
At a quarter to six the gauge read thirty-six.

**Taavi Brandt**  
That's my line. All crews off the walls, off the Marrick track, behind the car park wall. Leave the strip. Go.

They came off in the order he had given them, the wet band and the black walls left standing behind them like a stage with nobody on it, and were over the car park wall with a few minutes in hand. Nobody went up the Marrick track.

The headfire arrived at six minutes to six. It did not come as a wave. It came as a noise, then as a colour on the underside of the smoke, then as a line of brightness across the whole west face of the hill with embers going over it like thrown seed. It reached the first wall. It looked over. Illuminara watched it do exactly what an old woman had said it would do, and find nothing for its mouth.

In the gully it was worse and better. The fire went down into the cut because the cut drew it. Illuminara kept her eyes on the head of the cut and on the two banks, as she had told him she would, and said what she saw aloud so that he could hear it.

**Illuminara**  
Slowing. Banks clear.

The wet band took it to a crawl; it tried both banks and found them combed and black, and no flame stood on either one for longer than it took to be seen. For forty minutes it hissed and leaned and spat at the stone. Then it ran out of road.

Not everything held. The two Marrick cottages lay forty metres beyond the fence where the break ended, exactly where she had marked the edge of her water, and there had been neither time nor crew to carry it further. A gust took an ember across the last wall at ten past six. Joss started along the wall toward the tanker parked at the foot of the Marrick track.

**Taavi Brandt**  
No. They're empty. Let them go.

**Joss Marren**  
Chief, they're Hennie's—

**Taavi Brandt**  
They're stone and slates. Hennie's in the school hall with his dog. This wall is the line, and that track is the wrong side of it. If I send one lad up it and the wind veers again, I've done Calder in a new place. Let them go, Joss.

They went up like paper lanterns, one and then the other, and the whole crew watched them in a silence that Illuminara did not interrupt. Below them the village lay dark and standing. Three hundred roofs. A school with its windows reflecting something that was no longer a threat.

scenes.title: What Remained
paragraphs: *Corrandon cottage, kitchen · 21:40*

Constable Hale took the statement at the kitchen table with her hat on her knee and was careful to write only what she was told. Ivet gave it with her bandaged hand flat on the wood. When it was done Hale put away her pen and said nothing about permits, because there was a chief in the doorway and it was his to say.

**Taavi Brandt**  
The Marrick cottages are ash. The test burn was lit without a licence, on my say, against the district's written order. I'll answer for both. I'll answer, too, for the look I gave an old woman at midday.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
You gave me a perfectly good look. I'd have given it to you.

**Taavi Brandt**  
My report starts with your map and ends with my abort line. The review can read it in that order.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
They'll fine me.

**Taavi Brandt**  
They may. I'll stand beside you at the hearing and carry your map in with me, with the gauge log and the times, and say what I saw on that wall and in that cut. That isn't a pardon. I can't give you one. It isn't a promise they'll adopt anything, either.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
I don't want a pardon. I want it taught.
Brandt turned his hat once in his hands. It was the nearest thing to hesitation the night had left him.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Then a trial, not a promise. Two of your walls first, my crews, in the dry month, my gauge in my hand and my line on the radio. The regional office can quarrel about the paper with a hillside that's still standing.
Ivet said nothing for a while. Edrin's map lay open under the lamp, drawn forty years ago in pencil on the back of a seed catalogue: every wall of Sorrel Gate, each lee shaded.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
Then I'll say what I'm giving, since you've said what you are. I don't light alone again. I light with your crew at my elbow, and when you call your signal my torch stops, and I won't need telling twice. And the gully goes on the map, in ink. Edrin said it burns itself. It burned itself because Hennie's goats kept it bare, and when the goats went nobody wrote the date on the rule. I want the date on it.

Illuminara drew one more line on the map at the north, a thin blue cut with an arrow, and wrote beside it, in her small precise hand, leat and wet band, comb downhill; one hill, one wind, one day. She turned the paper toward the old woman.

**Illuminara**  
Would you sign it with his name as well? It's the part he never had time to finish.
Ivet took the pencil in her bandaged hand, and wrote, slowly and without once pressing too hard, *Edrin Corrandon*, and under it, *and Ivet*.

critic_line: An old woman's forbidden firecraft, a chief's fatal memory and Illuminara's water model become a bounded, stoppable defence that saves Sorrel Gate because each of them is willing to find where their own map is wrong.

literary_score.method: Exact 50/50 mean of two independent READER_APPEAL_R1 reader judgments
shared_strengths: Strong dialogue-driven premise with humane characters, a clear idea (fire as firebreak, forgotten goats), and a costly, honest ending. Dense operational numbers in the middle and somewhat stiff, formal dialogue may slow some readers, but the stakes and ending land well.

A compelling practical mystery becomes a tense, humane test of inherited knowledge, scientific humility, and responsible command. Distinctive dialogue, vivid fire imagery, and meaningful consequences should strongly sustain this audience, though the dense operational measurements may briefly slow some readers.
shared_reservations: Reader attention was most at risk around: “She put her finger on his map, on the thin blue cut above the Marrick cottages, and gave him the numbers one at a time so that he could argue with each.”
Reader attention was most at risk around: “Two hundred and forty metres from the sluice to the Marrick fence, three terraces, the third at a hundred and eighty. Eleven minutes a hundred metres.”

translation_sl.title: OGENJ, KI JE VEDEL, KAKO GORETI
translation_sl.deck: Enainosemdesetletna ženska je na hribu, ki ga želi gasilska služba izprazniti, zanetila enainštirideset majhnih ognjev; da bi dokazali, da ima prav, morajo najti edino mesto, kjer je njen zemljevid napačen.
translation_sl.shape: Šest prizorov v enem popoldnevu in večeru: vzorec, razumljen kot zločin, kuhinja, kjer je vzorec pojasnjen, preizkus, ki ga načelnik lahko ustavi, jarek, ki ga ni požgal nihče, veter, ki se obrne ob pravem času, in poročilo, ki se začne z zemljevidom stare ženske.

scenes.title: Ožigi ob zidu
paragraphs: *Sorrel Gate, zgornje terase · 12:40*

Dim je stal na zahodnem grebenu, šest kilometrov stran, in se nagibal proti njim. Okrožje je Sorrel Gatu dalo čas do treh. Illuminara je dopoldne hodila po zgornjih terasah s tablico meritev potokov, zaradi česar jo je tja poslal regionalni urad za vode, pri prvem črnem madežu pa je to nehala početi.

Zdaj jih je bilo enainštirideset. Vsak je bil velik kakor namizni prt. Vsak je bil še topel, ko je dlan držala dva centimetra nad njim. Noben ni ležal v odprti travi. Vsak je bil na zavetrni strani suhozida ali ob robu terase in niti eden ni prešel kamna.
*Nekdo šteje veter,* je pomislila. *Nekdo neti samo tam, kjer je bil veter zavrnjen.*

Taavi Brandt je prišel po poti z neprižgano kapljično baklo za pasom, korak za njim pa mladi vodja ekipe Joss Marren. Bil je nekaj čez petdeset, širok in miren kakor človek, ki se je naučil besede porabiti nazadnje.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Nekdo mi od šestih zjutraj zažiga hrib. Za enajst ognjev vem, kaj so. Preostale bi pripisal isti roki.

**Illuminara**  
Enainštirideset. Vse sem prehodila.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Potem ste prehodili enainštirideset krajev, kjer bi ogenj človeku lahko ušel. Policistka Hale je pri cerkvi z nalogom za Ivet Corrandon. Stara je enainosemdeset let, mojim ekipam noče odpreti vrat, ob mraku pa jo sam odnesem po tej cesti. Raje bi videl, da gre peš.

**Illuminara**  
Poglejte, kje so, načelnik. Ne kdo jih je naredil.
Pogledal je, ker je bil pravičen in ker je to rekla tiho. Pogledal je najbližji madež in zid nad njim ter za dolžino enega vdiha ni rekel ničesar.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Calder Fold. Pred devetimi leti. Zanetil sem protipožig, zakonit in podpisan, v vetru, ki se je štiri ure vedel pravilno. V peti se je obrnil, ogenj je zajel pot, nato skedenj, v skednju pa je spal človek. Aldous Penn. Previdni ognji ubijajo ljudi. Neprevidni ne trajajo dovolj dolgo.

**Illuminara**  
Potem ne bom trdila, da je previdna. Vprašala bom, ali ima prav, in poiskala merilo, ki lahko odgovori, ne da bi moral kdor koli od naju čemur koli verjeti. Naj najprej govorim z njo.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Do dveh. Ob dveh začnejo polniti avtobuse in takrat bo v enem od njih ali na moji rami.

scenes.title: Čemu je bil namenjen hrib
paragraphs: *Koča Corrandonovih, kuhinja · 13:15*

Vrata niso bila zaklenjena. Illuminara je vseeno potrkala in glas za lesom ji je povedal, da nikoli niso, da ljudje samo verjamejo, da so, ter da lahko vstopi, če je dovolj pametna, da si obriše čevlje.

Ivet Corrandon je sedela za mizo s pepelom do komolcev, škatlico vžigalic ob desni roki in črnotrnovko ob stolu. Čez njeno levo dlan je potekal za prst širok žulj. Imela je obraz nekoga, ki je imel dolgo prav brez pomoči kogar koli.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
Vi ste vodno dekle. Rekli so, da je na mojih zidovih vodno dekle z napravo.

**Illuminara**  
Sem modelarka voda. Naprava je tablica in večinoma šteje potoke. Smem sesti?

**Ivet Corrandon**  
Če ste me prišli odpeljat na avtobus, lahko sedete na tla.

**Illuminara**  
Nimam pooblastila, da bi vas kamor koli odpeljala. Prišla sem vprašat o zidu na vrhu Pellamovega polja.

Stara ženska jo je nekaj časa gledala. Illuminara je med čakanjem vzela čisto krpo s kredence in z očmi vprašala za roko. Vprašanje lahko počaka, žulj pa ne. Ivet ji je dovolila, sprva odkrito sumničavo, nato pa počasi manj.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
Leta štiriinosemdeset je v tej kuhinji stal gozdar in mojemu Edrinu povedal, da se hriba ne sme požigati, da tega ne sme nihče in nikoli, ter mu vzel papir, ki je govoril, da smeva. Edrina so oglobili. Teden dni ni spregovoril. Štirideset let živimo pod hribom, ki ne more početi drugega kot rasti.

**Illuminara**  
Vi pa ste požigali naprej.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
Po malem. Ob koncu mokrega obdobja, na zavetrni strani zidov. Edrin je temu rekel česanje. Ogenj, ki pride čez greben, je lačen in požre vse med seboj in naslednjo stvarjo, ki jo lahko poje. Zavetrje zidu počesite do črnega in čelni požar pride do kamna, pogleda čez ter ne najde ničesar za svoja usta. Zid brez črnine za seboj je samo kup kamenja.

**Illuminara**  
Zakaj potem niste povedali načelniku?

**Ivet Corrandon**  
Nekoč je zažgal hrib in človek je umrl. Prebrala sem v časopisu. Slišal bo stara ženska, slišal bo odgovornost, zidu pa ne bo slišal.
Rekla je brez krutosti, kakor bi povedala težo štruce. Illuminara se v tej kuhinji doslej ni motila o ničemer in slutila je, da to ne bo trajalo.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
Pa vi. Vaša naprava še nikoli ni vohala pobočja ob štirih popoldne. Nikoli ni stala tam, kjer si zrak premisli.

**Illuminara**  
Ne, ni. Zato mi povejte, kje je vaš zemljevid napačen. Raje bi to odkrila tukaj kakor na grebenu.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
Nikjer.
Tišina je trajala dovolj dolgo, da je kotliček tiktaknil. Ivet je pogledala oskrbljeno roko, palico in okno.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
Na severu. Jarek nad Marrickovima kočama. Zmanjkalo mi je kolena. Edrin jarka nikoli ni česal. Rekel je, da se požge sam. Nato o njem ni rekel niti besede več, jaz pa nisem nikoli vprašala.

Nekaj se je v Illuminari tiho obrnilo, kakor ključ v ključavnici, na katero se je naslanjala tri tedne. Jarek je bil stari kamniti razbremenilni kanal, poplavna struga, ki jo je modelirala za urad za vode. Vsaka nevihta, ki jo je simulirala, je šla po tistem rezu kakor nit skozi šivankino uho. *Voda ga najde. In vse drugo, kar hoče navzdol, tudi.*

**Illuminara**  
Gospa Corrandon, bi mi povedali vrstni red, po katerem požigate? Ne razlogov. Vrstni red. Načelniku ga bom prinesla kot nekaj, kar lahko preizkusi s svojo baklo in po svoji odločitvi.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
In če njegov preizkus pokaže, da sem neumna?

**Illuminara**  
Potem se napaka neumne ženske popravi na tridesetih metrih namesto napaka vasi na tristo. V obeh primerih zmaga hrib.

scenes.title: Preizkus, ki ga je lahko ustavil
paragraphs: *Šola v Sorrel Gatu, poveljniško mesto · 14:05*

Na parkirišču sta z odprtimi vrati brnela dva avtobusa. Brandt je stal nad zložljivo mizo, na kateri so štirje kamni držali zemljevid okrožja, in ni dvignil pogleda, dokler ni svoje tablice položila čez njegovo okrožje. Za njegovim ramenom je Joss Marren nalagal kolut s cevjo in se trudil, da ne bi poslušal.

**Illuminara**  
Ne neti ognjev. Češe zavetrno stran vsakega zidu, da čelni požar za kamnom nima česa pojesti. To je požarna pregrada, narisana z ognjem. Stara je štirideset let in država jo je vsa ta leta prepovedovala.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Tako pravi ona.

**Illuminara**  
Tako pravijo zidovi. Berem jih kot poti obremenitve, pot obremenitve pa je razlaga in ona bi lahko imela prav po naključju. Zato ne prosim, da ji verjamete. Prosim za en odsek. Trideset metrov vzhodnega zidu, vaša ekipa, vaša bakla, vaša cev za njim. Če ogenj v zavetrju ne ugasne sam, ga pogasite in izgubili smo dvajset minut.

**Taavi Brandt**  
In če ugasne sam, sem se nekaj naučil o enem zidu. Čelni požar ni en zid.

**Illuminara**  
Ne. Je pa način, da naključje spremenimo v meritev. Prosila bi vas, da ob njem pretehtate še nekaj, ker mislim, da ima glede zidov prav, bojim pa se kraja, ki ga ni požgala.
Dolgo si je vzel. Voznik avtobusa je zakašljal. Zunaj je ženska poimensko štela otroke iz šole v prvi avtobus in pravilno izgovorila vsako ime.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Potem so te odločitve moje. Avtobusi gredo ob treh, vsi, in nihče ne izstopi. Kdor ni na avtobusu, je v ekipi ali na cisterni. Veter se bo okoli dvajset do šestih obrnil na jugozahod. Imam eno številko, ki ima v vsaki uri drugo nalogo. Preden prižgemo baklo, petintrideset na grebenskem merilniku prekliče požig. Ko je bakla prižgana in se pas ohladi, sunek nad petintrideset ali ena žerjavica čez zid pomeni, da nihče ne prižge ničesar več: vse ekipe zapustijo zidove in Marrickovo pot ter se postavijo za zid parkirišča, črnina in mokrota pa opravita svoje. Čelnega požara ne lovim s cevjo. Ženska pa ostane, kjer jo vidim. Brez lisic. Ob moji rami.

**Illuminara**  
To bo želela. Želela bo vedeti, kaj opazuje.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Hale bo njeno izjavo vzela pozneje. Ni pomiloščena. Če gre to narobe s hitrostjo Calderja, hočem, da piše, da sem jo slišal in se odločil, ne da me je prevarala.
Ivet je prišla do vrat parkirišča, ne da bi jo kdo opazil, kar je pri enainosemdesetih letih in s palico zahtevalo talent. Stala je v podboju in slišala zadnji del.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
Nikoli nisem prosila za pomilostitev, načelnik.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Ne. Pravijo mi, da nikoli niste nikogar prosili za nič. Večina težave je prav v tem.

scenes.title: Jarek
paragraphs: *Vzhodni zid, nato začetek jarka · 16:05*

Joss Marren je deset čez štiri prižgal trideset metrov zavetrja, Brandt je čepel ob njegovem komolcu, Ivet pa je na poti nad njima sedela na izposojenem zložljivem stolu s palico čez kolena kakor z mečem, ki se ga je odločila ne izvleči. Plamen se je splazil tri korake po travi. Legel je ob kamen in ugasnil.
Nihče ni nič rekel. Drugi prehod malo dlje: enako. Joss je pogledal načelnika. Brandt je vtaknil dva prsta v črnino in ju pustil tam.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Hladno.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
Seveda je hladno. Ni imelo česa prositi.

Nato je dim zadnjega majhnega madeža storil nekaj, na kar je Illuminara čakala in glede česar ni uživala, da ima prav. Ni se dvignil. Po tleh je zdrsnil vstran, tanek in siv, se nagibal proti severu ter šel v ustje jarka nad Marrickovima kočama kakor voda v odtok.

**Illuminara**  
Načelnik, poglejte dim. To je moj potok. Jarek je stari razbremenilni kanal in za zrak ima enako obliko kakor za vodo. Ko se veter ob dvajset do šestih obrne na jugozahod, čelni požar ne bo prišel nad vas čez zidove, ki jih je prečesala. Prišel bo na edini kraj, ki za seboj nima črnine, kanal pa ga bo odnesel naravnost po rezu in čez zgornjo teraso.

**Taavi Brandt**  
V šolo in Marrickovi koči.

**Illuminara**  
V oboje. In pri zidu se ne bo ustavil, ker za tem zidom štirideset let nihče ni ničesar požgal.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
Edrin je rekel, da se požge sam.

**Illuminara**  
Kdaj je to rekel?

**Ivet Corrandon**  
Leto po tem, ko so odšle koze. Hennie Marrick jih je v tistem rezu pasel šestdeset in pojedle so vse do gline. Edrin je povedal, kar je videl. Ni pa povedal, da so koze požigale namesto nas.
Prvič je videla staro žensko presenečeno in iz vljudnosti ni odvrnila pogleda. Štirideset let pravila, ki je bilo pravilno na dan, ko je bilo izrečeno.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Suhega ne morem požgati nazaj. Ne, ko je čelni požar oddaljen dve uri. Suho gorivo v rezu s takim vlekom — sam bi prižgal svoj dimnik.

**Illuminara**  
Potem ga ne požgite suhega. Na začetku kanala je zapornica in potok še teče. Štirideset litrov na sekundo za mokri pas po dnu reza in čez oba bregova, na vsaki strani pa rob, ki ga vaša ekipa počasi prečeše navzdol, kakor gospa Corrandon. Moker pas, črn pas, zid. Ogenj ima na eni strani reko in na drugi kamen ter lahko gre samo ven.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Navzdol. Ne navzgor. V zapiskih ste rekli navzgor.

**Illuminara**  
Sem.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Navzgor mu naredite klančino. V tridesetih letih nisem nikoli prižigal po pobočju navzgor. Navzdol mora plamen delati za vsak meter.

**Illuminara**  
Navzdol. Hvala.
Prst je položila na njegov zemljevid, na tanki modri rez nad Marrickovima kočama, in mu številke podala drugo za drugo, da se je lahko prepiral z vsako posebej.

**Illuminara**  
Od zapornice do Marrickove ograje je dvesto štirideset metrov, tri terase, tretja pri sto osemdesetih. Enajst minut na sto metrov. Zapornico odprite deset do petih in mokra fronta bo deset čez za tretjo teraso. Če ne bo, nihče ne prižge robov in ekipe gredo k zidu parkirišča. To je edini znak odpovedi in pride, preden pride kakršen koli ogenj. Mokro in črno lahko segata do ograje in niti metra dlje. Koči sta štirideset metrov za njo, onkraj vse vode, ki jo lahko pripeljem. Raje to povem zdaj, kakor da bi vi odkrili ob šestih.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Kaj pa zid, ki smo ga pravkar požgali?

**Illuminara**  
Dokazuje en zid. Zato zaupam robovom in ne hribu. Hrib bom spoznala, ko nam pove jarek, in povedala vam bom, kaj opazovati. Če imam prav, bo čelni požar vstopil na začetku reza in se na mokrem pasu upočasnil do plazenja. Če nimam, se ne bo upočasnil in na bregu boste videli stati plamen. Oba ga lahko vidiva izza zidu parkirišča.

Kolo na začetku zapornice se ni zavrtelo že od časa, preden je Illuminara prišla v okrožje. Joss, dva Brandtova prostovoljca in kos gradbene cevi za vzvod so ga morali premakniti skupaj; ona je stala ob njih z uro in jih glasno vodila skozi delo, kakor se šteje ženski med porodom. Deset do petih se je kamnito grlo napolnilo in rez je začel govoriti.
Deset čez pet je mokra fronta sijala za tretjo teraso, grebenski merilnik pa je kazal osemnajst. Brandt je pogledal eno številko in nato drugo.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Prižgite.
Joss je s počasno baklo šel po vzhodnem bregu navzdol, druga ekipa pa po zahodnem; hodili so navzdol in plamen je moral delati za vsak meter.

scenes.title: Veter se obrne
paragraphs: *Zid parkirišča pod jarkom · 17:39*
Veter se je obrnil minuto prezgodaj.

Prišel je z zahoda kakor vrata, ki se odprejo v dolgi hiši, in dim, ki se je tri ure nagibal proti severu, se je vzravnal, premislil ter nagnil v drugo smer. Grebenski merilnik na Brandtovem radiu je pokazal devetindvajset, nato triintrideset. Njegove ekipe so bile še na svojih črtah: črnina za vsakim zidom, mokri pas, ki je sijal po dnu reza, in prečesan rob na vsaki strani, kjer so še tiktakale zadnje žerjavice Jossove počasne bakle.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Štiriintrideset. Ničesar več ni treba prižgati, zato zdaj šteje druga polovica moje številke. Še ena in se umaknejo, hodijo in ne sprašujejo. Joss, povej jim številko. Hočem, da so že obrnjeni.
Petnajst do šestih je merilnik pokazal šestintrideset.

**Taavi Brandt**  
To je moja meja. Vse ekipe z zidov, z Marrickove poti, za zid parkirišča. Pustite pas. Pojdite.

Umaknili so se v vrstnem redu, ki jim ga je določil, za njimi pa so mokri pas in črni zidovi ostali kakor oder brez igralcev; čez zid parkirišča so prišli z nekaj minutami rezerve. Nihče ni šel po Marrickovi poti navzgor.

Čelni požar je prispel šest minut pred šesto. Ni prišel kakor val. Prišel je kot hrup, nato kot barva na spodnji strani dima, nato kot črta svetlobe čez vse zahodno lice hriba, žerjavice pa so letele čeznjo kakor vrženo seme. Dosegel je prvi zid. Pogledal je čez. Illuminara je opazovala, kako naredi natanko to, kar je napovedala stara ženska, in ne najde ničesar za svoja usta.

V jarku je bilo slabše in boljše. Ogenj je šel v rez, ker ga je rez vlekel. Illuminara je gledala začetek reza in oba bregova, kakor mu je obljubila, ter na glas govorila, kar je videla, da jo je lahko slišal.

**Illuminara**  
Upočasnjuje se. Bregova sta čista.

Mokri pas ga je upočasnil do plazenja; poskusil je oba bregova in našel prečesana ter črna, noben plamen pa na nobenem ni stal dlje, kakor je trajalo, da so ga opazili. Štirideset minut je sikal, se nagibal in pljuval v kamen. Nato mu je zmanjkalo poti.

Ni zdržalo vse. Marrickovi koči sta ležali štirideset metrov za ograjo, kjer se je pregrada končala, natanko tam, kjer je označila rob svoje vode; ne časa ne ekipe ni bilo, da bi jo podaljšali. Deset čez šest je sunek odnesel žerjavico čez zadnji zid. Joss je ob zidu krenil proti cisterni, parkirani ob vznožju Marrickove poti.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Ne. Prazni sta. Pustite ju.

**Joss Marren**  
Načelnik, Henniejevi sta —

**Taavi Brandt**  
Iz kamna in skrilavca sta. Hennie je v šolski dvorani s svojim psom. Ta zid je meja, tista pot pa je na njeni napačni strani. Če po njej pošljem enega fanta in se veter spet obrne, sem Calder ponovil drugje. Pusti ju, Joss.

Zagoreli sta kakor papirnati svetilki, ena in nato druga, vsa ekipa pa ju je opazovala v tišini, ki je Illuminara ni prekinila. Pod njimi je vas stala temna in cela. Tristo streh. Šola, katere okna so odsevala nekaj, kar ni bilo več grožnja.

scenes.title: Kar je ostalo
paragraphs: *Koča Corrandonovih, kuhinja · 21:40*

Policistka Hale je za kuhinjsko mizo vzela izjavo s klobukom na kolenu in skrbno zapisala samo to, kar ji je bilo povedano. Ivet jo je podala z obvezano roko, položeno plosko na les. Ko je končala, je Hale pospravila pero in o dovoljenjih ni rekla ničesar, ker je v vratih stal načelnik in je moral govoriti on.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Marrickovi koči sta pepel. Preizkusni požig je bil zaneten brez dovoljenja, po moji odločitvi in v nasprotju s pisnim ukazom okrožja. Odgovarjal bom za oboje. Tudi za pogled, ki sem ga opoldne namenil stari ženski.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
Namenili ste mi povsem primeren pogled. Sama bi vam dala enakega.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Moje poročilo se začne z vašim zemljevidom in konča z mojo mejo za prekinitev. Pregledovalci ga lahko berejo v tem vrstnem redu.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
Oglobili me bodo.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Morda. Na zaslišanju bom stal ob vas, prinesel vaš zemljevid, dnevnik merilnika in čase ter povedal, kaj sem videl pri tistem zidu in v tistem rezu. To ni pomilostitev. Ne morem vam je dati. Tudi obljuba ni, da bodo kar koli sprejeli.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
Nočem pomilostitve. Hočem, da se tega učijo.
Brandt je klobuk enkrat obrnil v rokah. To je bilo še najbližje omahovanju, kar mu ga je pustila noč.

**Taavi Brandt**  
Potem preizkus, ne obljuba. Najprej dva vaša zidova, moje ekipe, v suhem mesecu, moj merilnik v roki in moja meja po radiu. Regionalni urad se lahko o papirjih prepira s hribom, ki še vedno stoji.

Ivet nekaj časa ni rekla ničesar. Edrinov zemljevid je ležal odprt pod svetilko, narisan pred štiridesetimi leti s svinčnikom na hrbtni strani semenskega kataloga: vsak zid Sorrel Gata, vsako zavetrje osenčeno.

**Ivet Corrandon**  
Potem bom povedala, kaj dajem jaz, saj ste vi povedali, kaj dajete vi. Sama ne prižigam več. Prižigam z vašo ekipo ob komolcu, in ko sporočite svoj znak, moja bakla ugasne, dvakrat pa mi ne bo treba povedati. Jarek gre na zemljevid, s črnilom. Edrin je rekel, da se požge sam. Sam se je požgal, ker so ga Henniejeve koze ohranjale golega, ko pa so koze odšle, nihče ni zapisal datuma na pravilo. Hočem, da je datum na njem.

Illuminara je na severu zemljevida narisala še eno črto, tanek moder rez s puščico, in ob njem s svojo drobno, natančno pisavo zapisala: *kanal in mokri pas, češi navzdol; en hrib, en veter, en dan.* Papir je obrnila proti stari ženski.

**Illuminara**  
Bi ga podpisali tudi z njegovim imenom? To je del, ki ga ni imel časa dokončati.
Ivet je z obvezano roko vzela svinčnik in počasi, ne da bi enkrat samkrat pritisnila premočno, napisala *Edrin Corrandon*, pod to pa *in Ivet*.

translation_sl.critic_line: Prepovedana veščina požiganja stare ženske, načelnikov smrtonosni spomin in Illuminaren model voda postanejo omejena, ustavljiva obramba, ki reši Sorrel Gate, ker je vsak od njih pripravljen odkriti, kje je napačen njegov lastni zemljevid.
